headline: A vendor survey says companies doubled their AI agents in a quarter while barely half of them are monitored.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: paid vendor content on TechCrunch, survey data from April 2026, no independent check.
importance_line: Employees and customers of banks and telecoms are the ones exposed when unmonitored agents act on their data, but the numbers come from a vendor selling the fix and have had no independent review.
summary: Gravitee, an API-management company that now sells tools to govern AI agents, says in a sponsored post on TechCrunch that its survey of 750 executives found the typical company's agent count rose from 26-50 to 76-100 in a single quarter, that only about half of those agents are monitored, and that 54 percent of organizations had or suspected an agent-related security or privacy incident in the past year. The data is from April 2026 and comes from a vendor with a product to sell, so it is a signal to watch rather than an independent finding.
notes: Paid placement (TC Brand Studio); TechCrunch is not the source. Category moved from MOD to SEC because the subject is agent security and governance. Report release date not stated; survey fieldwork April 2026.
